items.title: Tutti gli sconti Tineco per la Festa delle Offerte Prime. Fino a oltre 200 euro di risparmio
items.summary: Dal 6 al 7 ottobre Tineco porta su Amazon una selezione di lavapavimenti, aspirapolvere e soluzioni per tappeti con prezzi promozionali. Ecco cinque modelli da conoscere e le loro caratteristiche principali ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
La Festa delle Offerte Prime è l'occasione giusta per passare a una nuova lavapavimenti o a un nuovo aspirapolvere. Le promozioni previste da Tineco sono davvero ottime, con sconti che possono superare i 200 euro rispetto al prezzo di listino.

Il 6 e il 7 ottobre su Amazon troverai in sconto: FLOOR ONE S9 Artist Boost Steam, FLOOR ONE S9 Artist Steam Pro, FLOOR ONE S7 Stretch Ultra, PURE ONE A70S e CARPET ONE Cruiser.

Le offerte di ottobre arrivano in un momento in cui Tineco continua ad ampliare una categoria sulla quale lavora ormai da diversi anni. Da quando nel 2020 ha contribuito alla diffusione delle lavapavimenti intelligenti con FLOOR ONE S1, uno dei primi prodotti di questo tipo arrivati sul mercato, non si è più fermata. Da allora ha sviluppato la gamma di prodotti per la pulizia introducendo progressivamente sensori, sistemi automatici di gestione dell’acqua, funzioni per l’autopulizia e soluzioni dedicate alla manutenzione del dispositivo. Affinché ogni nuova generazione apporti novità concrete, che semplifichino la vita quotidiana delle persone per le attività di pulizia. Con un mantra che guidasse il proprio lavoro: Tineco Floor Washer: Every Generation, A New Definition. Ogni generazione, un nuovo standard.

Tineco è stata il primo marchio al mondo per volume di vendite retail nel segmento degli aspirapolvere wet & dry per uso domestico per quattro anni consecutivi, dal 2022 al 2025. In più, dispone di uno dei primi laboratori del settore accreditati CNAS e partecipa allo sviluppo di standard internazionali IEC e ASTM.

Per chi cerca una lavapavimenti pensata anche per intervenire sulle macchie più ostinate, una delle proposte principali è FLOOR ONE S9 Artist Boost Steam. Il modello mette al centro il sistema a vapore e, in particolare, la funzione BoostSteam.

Alla prima attivazione il vapore a 230° C viene generato in 20 secondi; per le erogazioni successive l’attesa scende a circa cinque secondi. L’utente può richiamare rapidamente un getto più intenso quando incontra sporco particolarmente difficile. Questa funzione è ideale per i luoghi della casa, come la cucina, dove spesso i pavimenti si sporcano di residui grassi, più difficili da rimuovere: bastano pochi secondi per sciogliere la macchia e igienizzare le superfici.

Alla funzione BoostSteam si affianca ReverseScrub: il rullo spazzola si muove all’inverso per un lavoro mirato per rimuovere ogni tipo di macchia. A cui si aggiunge la potente aspirazione da 25.000 Pa.

Inoltre, il design HyperStretch - ormai un marchio di fabbrica di tanti prodotti della gamma di Tineco - consente di reclinare la lavapavimenti fino a 180°, per passare con più agilità sotto letti, divani e mobili bassi. Terminata la pulizia, il sistema FlashDry gestisce l’autopulizia e l’asciugatura interna con aria calda a 110° C.

Durante la Festa delle Offerte Prime, FLOOR ONE S9 Artist Boost Steam passa dal prezzo di listino di 699 euro a 599 euro.

FLOOR ONE S9 Artist Steam Pro si rivolge invece a chi vuole combinare aspirazione e lavaggio a vapore nella normale pulizia delle superfici dure. In questo caso Tineco utilizza la tecnologia HyperSteam a 160° C, che serve a sciogliere macchie e sporco aderente al pavimento assicurandosi che la temperatura di uscita non scenda sotto i 99° C.

Il sistema DualBlock interviene invece su capelli e peli, limitandone l’accumulo e i grovigli attorno al rullo. Anche FLOOR ONE S9 Artist Steam Pro adotta la tecnologia ReverseScrub, per sfruttare l’inversione del rullo spazzola per rimuovere le macchine più ostinate.

Il design Lay-Flat permette di reclinare la macchina fino a 180°, così da pulire più facilmente sotto mobili e arredi senza doverli spostare. In più, la spazzola è stata disegnata in modo ottimizzato, così che possa aderire ai bordi e non lasciare tracce di sporco e polvere. E per agevolare ancora di più le operazioni di pulizia, FLOOR One S9 Artist Steam Pro integra la collaudata tecnologia SmoothDrive, che aiuta nella spinta della lavapavimenti in avanti o nella rotazione negli angoli stretti, agevolando i movimenti e riducendo l’affaticamento. Anche il serbatoio dell’acqua è stato posizionato per aggiungere peso alla testina della spazzola e quindi ottenere una maggiore potenza di pulizia e ridurre lo sforzo.

Il prezzo di listino di FLOOR ONE S9 Artist Steam Pro è di 849 euro, mentre durante la promozione scende a 699 euro.

Non tutte le esigenze richiedono il vapore. Per chi cerca soprattutto una lavapavimenti flessibile per l’utilizzo quotidiano, Tineco propone FLOOR ONE S7 Stretch Ultra. Il modello utilizza la tecnologia MHCBS, che mantiene un flusso continuo di acqua pulita sul rullo e separa quella sporca durante il funzionamento: così dopo il passaggio i pavimenti restano davvero puliti. Il sistema interviene sul rullo fino a 450 volte al minuto, con l’obiettivo di evitare che lo sporco raccolto venga nuovamente trascinato sul pavimento.

Uno degli elementi più pratici è ancora una volta il design reclinabile a 180°. La macchina può raggiungere un’altezza minima di circa 13 centimetri, facilitando la pulizia sotto letti, divani e mobili. Anche in questa posizione le acque reflue vengono separate in tre camere distinte e senza compromettere la potenza di aspirazione. Anche su S7 Stretch Ultra il serbatoio dell’acqua serve ad aumentare la pressione sul pavimento: ciò migliora la qualità della pulizia e del lavaggio e riduce l’affaticamento, perché aiuta a sostenere il peso della lavapavimenti.

Il sistema DualBlock è progettato per contrastare i grovigli di capelli, mentre il ciclo di manutenzione automatica combina un autolavaggio di circa due minuti con un’asciugatura interna a 85° C della durata di cinque minuti. L’autonomia può raggiungere 50 minuti, rendendola adatta anche a sessioni di pulizia estese.

Per la Festa delle Offerte Prime, lo sconto sul FLOOR ONE S7 Stretch Ultra è notevole: da 499 euro passa a 279 euro.

La selezione Tineco non comprende soltanto lavapavimenti. PURE ONE A70S è un aspirapolvere senza fili pensato per adattarsi a superfici e situazioni differenti. La potenza di aspirazione arriva fino a 270 AW, mentre l’autonomia raggiunge 110 minuti.

Il sistema ClogLess è pensato per favorire il passaggio continuo di sporco e detriti, mentre la spazzola ZeroTangle riduce il problema di capelli e peli che tendono ad avvolgersi attorno al rullo. Inoltre, una luce verde con apertura a 120° aiuta a rendere più visibile la polvere sul pavimento.

Per raggiungere le zone sotto mobili e letti, PURE ONE A70S utilizza infine un tubo pieghevole fino a 180°, evitando di dover inclinare eccessivamente il corpo durante la pulizia.

Il prezzo promozionale del PURE ONE A70S previsto per la Festa delle Offerte Prime è di 349 euro, rispetto ai 399 euro di listino.

Tappeti e moquette richiedono un trattamento diverso rispetto ai normali pavimenti duri, soprattutto perché alla rimozione dello sporco si aggiunge il problema dell’umidità residua.

CARPET ONE Cruiser nasce proprio per questo tipo di superficie. La macchina raggiunge una potenza di aspirazione fino a 130 W e utilizza il sistema DualCore PowerDry con aria calda a 75° C. La spazzola rotante lavora a una velocità fino a 3000 giri al minuto.

Il sistema DrySense controlla in tempo reale l’umidità e la temperatura per garantire un’asciugatura ottimale del tappeto, evitando il surriscaldamento e prolungando la durata. Per di più, è inclusa l’illuminazione dinamica per dare a colpo d’occhio un’indicazione sullo stato di asciugatura: quando la luce è azzurra, il tappeto è asciutto.

I sensori iLoop regolano in tempo reale il flusso dell’acqua e l’aspirazione in base al livello di sporco rilevato, così da adattare l’intervento alle diverse zone del tappeto (e ottimizzare l’autonomia). Inoltre, sono disponibili tre livelli di trazione SmoothPower (alto, medio e basso), mentre gli accessori inclusi permettono di intervenire anche sulle aree più difficili da raggiungere. Anche sul CARPET ONE Cruiser, Tineco ha scelto di ottimizzare il design riposizionando il serbatoio dell’acqua e alleggerire il manico: ciò riduce l’affaticamento, agevola i movimenti sul tappeto e fa risparmiare tempo.

Anche la manutenzione del dispositivo è automatizzata: FlashDry esegue un ciclo di lavaggio interno di circa due minuti seguito dall’asciugatura a 55° C per tre minuti.

CARPET ONE Cruiser viene proposto durante la promozione a 469 euro, contro un prezzo di listino di 699 euro.

items.title: La Russia torna ad agitare la minaccia nucleare
items.summary: Questa volta lo ha fatto contro la Nato, un modo per spaventare governi e opinione pubblica. E per distogliere l’attenzione dalla campagna devastante condotta contro l’Ucraina Leggi
items.content:
Attenzione, l’informazione che segue potrebbe provocare angoscia e panico, ed è esattamente l’obiettivo di chi l’ha diffusa, ovvero la Russia di Vladimir Putin. Le notizie destabilizzanti arrivano una dopo l’altra: prima il drone carico di esplosivi scoperto in un aeroporto tedesco; poi, il 28 settembre, l’accusa di sabotaggio rivolta dall’Estonia a Mosca. Infine, è arrivato il turno della Nato, che ha rivelato di aver ricevuto un documento con cui il Cremlino minaccia addirittura una guerra nucleare se gli eserciti occidentali dovessero occupare il territorio russo di Kaliningrad , situato tra la Polonia, la Lituania e il mar Baltico.

Kaliningrad è un’exclave, ovvero un pezzo di territorio che non è collegato al paese d’origine. La ragion d’essere dell’avvertimento russo alla Nato non è legata ad alcun fatto d’attualità. Che si sappia, infatti, non esistono preparativi di un attacco della Nato contro il territorio russo, “scomodamente” incuneato tra paesi ostili. La Nato ha risposto accusando la Russia di adottare una “retorica nucleare irresponsabile” e ribadendo di non avere alcuna mira su Kaliningrad.

L’obiettivo della manovra è puramente psicologico. Dalla prospettiva di Mosca, infatti, agitare episodicamente lo spettro nucleare serve a calmare gli ardori dei leader europei, spaventando le popolazioni del vecchio continente e rafforzando il fronte di chi vuole smettere di aiutare l’Ucraina.

Questa tattica è uno degli strumenti della “guerra ibrida” portata avanti dalla Russia, che negli ultimi anni ha registrato un’intensa escalation. Tra le frecce nella faretra del Cremlino ci sono naturalmente le operazioni clandestine classiche, come quelle che hanno colpito la Francia con le scritte antisemite sui muri di Parigi dopo il 7 ottobre. Ma non mancano le azioni più semplici e poco costose per seminare il panico e ottenere una grande copertura mediatica, come i sorvoli dei droni sugli aeroporti e le basi militari. Il rischio è vicino allo zero, ma l’effetto è notevole, anche perché ogni volta scatena una polemica sul tema “il nostro paese è un colabrodo incapace di difendersi”.

La novità, oggi, è il passaggio ad azioni più gravi: secondo le autorità tedesche, il drone scoperto a Lipsia avrebbe potuto provocare vittime, mentre il sabotaggio della Milrem Robotics in Estonia ha causato un incendio. A questo punto viene da chiedersi quali saranno le prossime evoluzioni.

A ogni tappa la Russia impara dalle nostre reazioni, sia quelle delle opinioni pubbliche di paesi che non vivono una guerra da decenni (e non hanno la minima intenzione di correre il rischio di combatterne una), sia quelle dei governi, costantemente indecisi tra minimizzare e drammatizzare.

Bisogna ammettere che la Russia è molto più esperta dei paesi europei in questa arte della guerra psicologica. La frammentazione dell’Europa in 27 stati, di cui alcuni sono in piena campagna elettorale, non facilita certo una reazione coerente.

Agitando la minaccia nucleare, Mosca risveglia la paura profonda di un dottor Stranamore con il dito sul bottone atomico a Mosca, anche se non è questo il caso.

Tra l’altro questo approccio è un modo per distogliere l’attenzione dalla campagna devastante condotta dalla Russia contro l’Ucraina. Il problema reale non è il destino di Kaliningrad, ma quello dei civili ucraini sotto le bombe.

items.title: Airbnb si trasforma: lAI cerca la casa e confronta gli alloggi
items.summary: Ricerca con AI, confronti automatici e nuove funzioni social arrivano su Airbnb.
items.content:
Alzi la mano chi non ha rischiato di impazzire nel tentativo di cercare una casa per le vacanze! Se poi abbiamo le idee confise, i parametri da incrociare sono tantissimi, a partire da destinazione, date, prezzo, numero di camere e servizi. E poi si inizia a guardare decine di annunci, per poi essere presi dallo sconforto.

Il prossimo passo delle piattaforme di viaggio è quindi abbastanza naturale, perché invece di costringerci a impostare ogni filtro, si vuole provare a capire direttamente cosa stiamo cercando. Ora che ha capito bene che direzione prendere, Airbnb sta iniziando a utilizzare seriamente l'intelligenza artificiale, e con il nuovo aggiornamento autunnale gli utenti possono attivare una ricerca AI e descrivere tramite testo o voce il tipo di sistemazione desiderata. Il sistema interpreta la richiesta e propone automaticamente filtri pertinenti.

Pensiamo ad esempio alla ricerca di qualcosa di adatto a un bambino, Airbnb può suggerire caratteristiche come culle, aree gioco, libri o giocattoli. L'AI viene utilizzata anche per mettere in evidenza gli aspetti di un alloggio più interessanti per quella specifica ricerca, così le case salvate nelle liste dei desideri potranno essere confrontate attraverso riepiloghi generati dall'intelligenza artificiale, che tengono conto anche delle recensioni. Tutte queste novità dovrebbero ridurre uno dei passaggi più noiosi della prenotazione, ossia aprire continuamente più annunci per capire quale risponda meglio alle proprie esigenze.

items.title: WhatsApp introduce nuovi controlli parentali per gli adolescenti
items.summary: Nuovi controlli per gruppi, Status, Canali e Meta AI sugli account degli adolescenti.
items.content:
Proteggere gli adolescenti sulle piattaforme di messaggistica è particolarmente complicato e delicato come argomento, anche perché bisogna cercare di offrire ai genitori strumenti sufficienti per intervenire quando serve, ma senza trasformare ogni conversazione dei figli in qualcosa da sorvegliare. Si tratta sicuramente di un equilibrio delicato tra sicurezza e privacy, che WhatsApp sta cercando di affrontare con una nuova serie di controlli parentali dedicati agli account dei teenager.

La novità più interessante riguarda ciò che i genitori potranno effettivamente gestire, sarà possibile limitare l'utilizzo dei Canali, decidere quali Status possono essere visualizzati e chi può vedere quelli pubblicati dall'adolescente. I controlli riguarderanno anche la foto del profilo e la possibilità di essere aggiunti ai gruppi, e proprio quest'ultimi ricevono alcune delle funzioni più particolari.

I genitori potranno ricevere una notifica quando il figlio entra o esce da un gruppo, ma anche quando quest'ultimo raggiunge determinate dimensioni come 30, 100 oppure 250 partecipanti. Si tratta sostanzialmente di un modo per segnalare soprattutto l'ingresso in comunità molto numerose, dove diventa più difficile sapere con chi si sta interagendo.

items.title: Google rilancia sullAI con il rilascio di Gemini 4 Argon | Tutte le novità
items.summary: Gemini 4 Argon punta su coding, autonomia e prezzi aggressivi per sfidare GPT-6 e Claude.
items.content:
Nel nuovo flusso di modelli si inserisce anche Google con la sua nuova evoluzione, e ormai appare evidente che la nuova battaglia in tema di AI non si gioca più soltanto sulla capacità di rispondere bene a una domanda. Il vero terreno di scontro sono ormai i compiti lunghi e complessi, quelli in cui un'AI deve lavorare per molto tempo, utilizzare strumenti e arrivare autonomamente a un risultato.

Gemini 4 Argon è il nuovo frontier model con cui Google prova a recuperare terreno su OpenAI e Anthropic, e come sempre sono stati snocciolati i primi numeri, piuttosto interessanti a dire il vero. Argon raggiunge il 77,9% su DeepSWE v1.1, benchmark dedicato ad attività di sviluppo software di lunga durata, e il 51,3% su AutomationBench di Zapier. Nel test LVBench, dedicato invece alla comprensione di video molto lunghi, arriva al 91,7%.

Secondo Google, questi risultati permettono ad Argon di superare GPT-6 Astra e Claude Opus 5.5 in diversi test, ma come sempre i benchmark raccontano soltanto una parte della storia.

items.title: Repubblica, un giornale nel mondo
items.summary: Nasce oggi Repubblica Europe, la sezione in lingua inglese del nostro sito
items.content:
Repubblica guarda lontano e vuole essere letta anche da lontano. Non è una frase fatta, è lo spirito con il quale nasce oggi Repubblica Europe, la sezione in lingua inglese del nostro sito, primo passo di una più ampia internazionalizzazione dell’offerta giornalistica.

Non una semplice traduzione dei pezzi già presenti sul sito ma la costruzione di una proposta informativa curata e non episodica, capace di conciliare le esigenze dell'aggiornamento digitale con quelle della solidità di contenuto, per rendere Repubblica sempre più un punto di riferimento non solo per i lettori italiani ma per chiunque nel mondo sia curioso della realtà e voglioso di buon giornalismo.

Repubblica Europe racconterà l’Italia a un pubblico attento alle novità del nostro Paese ma vuole anche essere uno spazio per raccontare il mondo dall’Italia, con le nostre firme, i migliori reportage, le interviste esclusive che sono da sempre patrimonio di Repubblica e hanno reso la testata conosciuta nel mondo per l’autorevolezza e la credibilità. Tutto secondo la lezione seguita da questo giornale nel suo primo mezzo secolo di vita: informare, capire, interpretare, guardare avanti.

In più, certo, ci sarà la miniera delle storie italiane: la politica, la cultura, l’innovazione, la moda, il design, i motori, il territorio e le sue meraviglie, il cibo.

Eccellenze e problemi, il meglio e il peggio, contro ogni stereotipo o tentazione nazionalista. Ce ne sono già fin troppe in circolazione. Già nel nome della testata, in quel rimando all’Europa, c’è la collocazione naturale di Repubblica e dell’Italia.

items.title: Roberto Vannacci: The General Who Flirts With Putin’s Russia — and Could Cost Meloni the Election
items.summary: In just three years, the former special forces commander who has no qualms about echoing Mussolini has gone from obscurity to the European Parliament and the leadership of a new far-right party. Behind his rise is a network of figures with ties to Moscow — and a political agenda with striking similarities to the Kremlin’s
items.content:
ROME – In Italy, there is a general who has no qualms about echoing Benito Mussolini. He says “Italy for Italians”, argues that homosexuals are “not normal”, wants to stop immigration, defend the traditional family and put country, identity and authority back at the heart of public life. His name is Roberto Vannacci, and in just three years he has become the latest phenomenon in Italian politics.

Until the summer of 2023, almost no one knew who he was. Today he is a member of the European Parliament and the founder of Futuro Nazionale, a far-right party of the kind gaining ground across Europe, which some polls already put in double digits. He has also become one of the most serious threats to Giorgia Meloni. The Italian prime minister is moving closer to his position on some issues, while remaining wary of the challenge posed by his rise. Vannacci is drawing support from the same right-wing electorate and could prove decisive at the next election.

But who is Roberto Vannacci, really? And how did a special forces general become, in such a short time, a political leader capable of splitting the Italian right?

Vannacci has his own theory: it all happened by chance. He had commanded elite units, served in Iraq and Afghanistan, led the Folgore Parachute Brigade and been military attaché at the Italian embassy in Moscow. On 10 August 2023, he self-published Il mondo al contrario ( The World Back to Front ) on Amazon.

The book already contained almost everything that defines Vannacci’s politics today: homosexuals described as “not normal”, attacks on feminism and multiculturalism, and a defence of the traditional family, national identity and a society based on order and authority. A week later, Repubblica reported what was in it. The book became a bestseller and the general a national figure.

But when Repubblica revisited the story, it found a more complex picture. Six months before the book appeared, when Vannacci was still unknown, someone had begun building a detailed Wikipedia biography for him. The Hockler73 account told Wikipedia editors that it was working “on behalf of the person concerned”. According to the fact-checking outlet Facta, the person behind the username was military analyst Tiziano Ciocchetti, who would later become Vannacci’s assistant at the European Parliament. The page was published in March 2023, five months before the book.

This is not evidence of some hidden operation. But it is the first indication that Vannacci’s emergence may have been less accidental than it appeared. And there is one place that keeps resurfacing in the general’s biography: Moscow.

Vannacci knows Moscow well. In 2021, he arrived in Russia as military attaché at the Italian embassy. John Foreman, then Britain’s defence attaché, told the Financial Times that Vannacci regarded Russia as a “partner” and believed confrontation with Moscow had to be avoided.

On the eve of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022, he did not believe it would happen. When Russian tanks crossed the border, he told the Italian ambassador, Giorgio Starace, that they would go through “like a knife through butter” and that Kyiv would fall quickly. The following May, he was expelled from Moscow along with other Italian diplomats, in retaliation for the expulsions ordered by Rome.

But Russia has never disappeared from his story. Repubblica has reconstructed the network of figures now in the general’s orbit. There is Eliseo Bertolasi, who in 2025 received the Order of Friendship directly from Vladimir Putin. Antonio Imperatore is active in the “Friends of Imperial Russia – Third Rome”, whose members have been received by the Russian consul in Milan. Roberto Jonghi Lavarini is a regular visitor to the consulate and is close to Aleksandr Dugin, the ultranationalist philosopher and theorist of Eurasianism. Giovanni Trombetta has been identified as another of Dugin’s contacts in Italy. In Rome, the social media channels of a movement that later became part of the Futuro Nazionale orbit even posted a tribute last August to Darya Dugina, Dugin’s daughter, who was killed in a bombing in 2022.

But it is not only the people who are looking eastwards. There are the ideas, too.

Repubblica compared Futuro Nazionale’s programme with the one adopted at almost the same time by United Russia, Vladimir Putin’s party. There are numerous overlaps: the centrality of nation and sovereignty; the defence of traditional values against those imposed from outside; family and the birth rate as a guarantee of a people’s survival; economic and technological sovereignty; and immigration conditional on embracing national values.

Putin’s party says entry should be granted “only to those who share our values”; Futuro Nazionale makes “adherence to the values of our civilisation” a precondition. United Russia declares: “The more of us there are, the stronger our Motherland.” Vannacci says Italy must “start by reviving its birth rate”. Placed side by side, the two sets of positions show striking similarities.

And it was by following this same trail — where politics, Russia and the media intersect — that Repubblica found another story: that of Iana Permiakova.

A Russian who has lived in Italy for ten years, Permiakova is the wife of Luca Carleo, who was appointed deputy head of Futuro Nazionale in Lombardy and resigned 24 hours later because of his involvement in an investigation by Milan prosecutors.

Carleo was a senior figure at Ops Retail, formerly Netweek, a group that controls dozens of local newspapers and news websites. Permiakova also sat on its board of directors. Her CV states that from 2011 to 2016 she worked in the Press and Information Service Department of the government of the Russian Federation. Not at the Kremlin, therefore, but within the Russian government’s communications apparatus.

Permiakova has since resigned from the board and told Repubblica that she has no current ties with Moscow, apart from family ties with her parents, who still live in Russia.

The issue has drawn concern even within the Italian right. The Financial Times has described the general as a possible “Trojan horse” for Russian influence in Italy. Within Meloni’s Brothers of Italy party, the fear is summed up this way: “We wouldn’t want to end up having to answer to Moscow.”

Vannacci laughs off the accusations, denies receiving Kremlin funding or having secret ties, and acknowledges only that he has retained “friends and acquaintances” in Russia.

That, perhaps, is what makes his story more than simply an Italian political phenomenon: a general turned political leader; the old radical right meeting the new European populism; the pull of Putin’s Russia.

And one question — or rather, two — now hangs over Rome: how far can Roberto Vannacci go? And who is running alongside him?

items.title: Italian superyachts lead the way, but smaller builders struggle
items.summary: Genoa Boat Show opens: more than 1,000 boats go on display, from Sanlorenzo’s 1960s-inspired yacht to Capelli’s violin-shaped RIB. Luxury drives revenues to a record €8.6 billion, but the industry is moving at two speeds
items.content:
ROME – More than 1,000 boats on the water, 215 new launches and a record number of multihulls: the Genoa International Boat Show, which opens today in the Ligurian capital, is looking to regain momentum.

The industry is moving at two different speeds. Premium yachts and larger vessels continue to sustain the market, while smaller recreational boats are losing ground, held back by rising costs, a shortage of berths and international uncertainty. Italy remains the world leader in superyachts, but the industry faces mounting pressures and demand that is less buoyant than during the pandemic boom.

Held at Genoa’s Waterfront di Levante, designed by architect Renzo Piano, the show runs until Tuesday, October 6. The new dates are intended to prevent it from being squeezed between the Cannes Yachting Festival and the Monaco Yacht Show, give exhibitors more space and strengthen the international standing of the event, organised by Italy’s marine industry association, Confindustria Nautica.

The initial figures suggest the strategy is working: more than 1,000 boats announced, 215 new product launches, a 4% increase in the exhibition area occupied by boats on the water and a 28% rise in the number of multihulls, a new record for the Genoa show.

The number of large yachts and superyachts is also increasing. This is the segment that has proved most resilient in the face of the market slowdown.

The transformation is reflected in Living Made in Italy, a new exhibition area dedicated to Italian-built yachts over 24 metres, featuring vessels ranging from 35 to 50 metres.

Visitors will be able to explore luxury and premium yachts, with a focus on customisation, technology and sophisticated onboard living, alongside leading Italian design names including Venini, Riflessi and Leonardo.

The future of yachting is taking shape through retro-inspired designs, asymmetric hulls and increasingly efficient solutions for reducing fuel consumption and emissions. Italian craftsmanship is another source of inspiration, including Cremona’s centuries-old tradition of violin-making.

Sanlorenzo is presenting SHE, a 25.5-metre yacht that reinterprets the Italian motor yachts of the 1960s. With no flybridge, soft, flowing lines, interiors designed by Lissoni that resemble a glass-walled penthouse and a stern that transforms into a terrace, SHE combines vintage inspiration with contemporary design.

Its Volvo Penta IPS hybrid propulsion system also allows it to operate in electric mode at low speeds.

The SL80A, meanwhile, uses an asymmetric design to create additional interior space and an expansive main saloon opening directly onto the sea.

Among the more unusual exhibits is Cantieri Capelli’s Stradivari 52, a 15.5-metre maxi RIB inspired by Cremona’s violin-making tradition.

The curve of its stern evokes a violin bow, while four lines recall the instrument’s strings.

Powered by four outboard engines delivering a combined 1,800 horsepower, it can reach speeds approaching 50 knots.

Azimut is bringing its distinctive brand of sophisticated Italian elegance to the show with the Grande 44M, a four-deck flagship featuring an owner’s suite on the upper deck and a private terrace.

More than 50% of its structure is made from carbon fibre, helping to reduce CO₂ emissions by up to 30%.

The Magellano 27M takes the crossover yacht concept a step further, combining a Dual Mode hull, the range required for long-distance cruising and elegant interiors designed by AMDL CIRCLE.

The Seadeck 9 is designed to bring passengers closer to nature. Its standout feature is a 60-square-metre Fun Island, complemented by sea-facing terraces, a swimming pool and light-filled interiors.

The Fly 70, which combines sporty performance with Italian comfort, introduces technology capable of cutting particulate emissions by 95% while significantly reducing onboard noise.

Its premieres include the Riva 56’ Rivale Super, a sportier evolution of an iconic model, and the Ferretti Yachts 720, designed to create a seamless connection between indoor and outdoor spaces.

The line-up also includes the Pershing 6X, Itama 54, Ferretti Yachts 580, wallypower50 and wallywhy200. At Berth H, the Pershing GTX116 introduces the brand’s new sport utility design language.

In the maxi RIB category, the muscular Novamarine Black Shiver 200 and 160 combine performance and safety with yacht-quality finishes.

Another standout is the Bluegame BGM75, described as a "monohull with two hulls". Its dimensions remain compatible with standard marina berths, while fuel consumption and power requirements are reduced by up to 40%. It also features an eight-metre-wide owner’s suite.

Also on display is the Prestige M8 Evo, built in Italy by France’s Groupe Beneteau at its Monfalcone shipyard in Friuli-Venezia Giulia.

It offers 270 square metres of usable space, a flybridge measuring approximately 50 square metres, fuel consumption and emissions reduced by half, and an estimated range of 1,000 nautical miles at eight knots.

Behind the impressive array of vessels on display, however, the industry is grappling with the end of the boom triggered by the pandemic.

The difficulties are particularly acute in the small and medium-sized boat market and the more affordable recreational boating segment.

Rising prices, higher raw material and energy costs, US tariffs and geopolitical tensions are all weighing on demand.

These pressures are compounded by a structural problem specific to Italy: a shortage of marina berths.

Marinas are often operating at full capacity, and the overall cost of owning even a small boat can exceed €10,000 a year, discouraging new buyers from entering the market.

Luxury yachts and medium-to-large vessels are holding up better, but they are not immune to market turbulence.

The impact is already visible in company accounts. Ferretti, for example, has had to revise its targets following its first-half results.

Then there is the The Italian Sea Group, which has been hit by a financial crisis amid extra costs and allegations of management irregularities.

Eleven non-binding offers have reportedly been submitted for the acquisition of individual business divisions or the entire group.

Names linked to the bidding include Azimut Benetti, Ferretti, Palumbo, Baglietto, Blackstone through Safe Harbor, and Asia Investment Holding.

The decisive stage is expected on October 19, when binding offers are due to be submitted.

According to Deloitte’s report The State of the Art of the Global Yachting Market 2026, the worldwide market for new boats was worth approximately €33.3 billion in 2025, down 2.1% from 2023 but still one and a half times its 2019 level.

Italy continues to outperform the global average. Domestic production is estimated at between €5.4 billion and €5.5 billion, an increase of around 7%, compared with a 3% contraction worldwide.

Italy’s market share has risen from 15% to 18%. In the superyacht sector, the country accounts for 56% of global production by volume and 36% by value.

The marine industry, however, extends well beyond shipyards.

According to Fondazione Symbola, the wider sector generated more than €13 billion in added value in 2024 and employed almost 168,000 people.

To attract younger generations and newcomers to boating, this year’s Genoa Boat Show will also introduce the Blue Arena at the city’s Palasport.

The new space will be dedicated to education and training, start-ups, maritime careers, sailing and opportunities for people taking their first steps into boating.

The show will also promote Italy’s D1 boating licence, which can be obtained from the age of 16.

items.title: Artist JR: “After us, the flood. That’s why my wave is sweeping across the Vatican”
items.summary: His monumental installation, Diluvium, covers the façade of the Vatican Apostolic Library in Rome, drawing attention to climate change. “Like Noah, we now have a duty to preserve humanity”
items.content:
ROME – JR quickly brushes aside the thought of exhibiting his work just a short distance from Michelangelo’s masterpieces. “I try not to think about it,” says the French artist, whose work spans photography, collage, graffiti and film. He was invited to create the first installation of the modern era inside the Vatican: Diluvium, a gigantic wave covering the façade of the Vatican Apostolic Library, as part of an exhibition inaugurated by the Pope himself.

“One thing is certain: my work is temporary, while Michelangelo’s is permanent. And that,” he says with a smile, “puts my ego in its place.”

The exhibition, AQVA, which runs until May 14, 2027, was created in collaboration with American typographer Bill Moran and Italian chef Fulvio Pierangelini. It is the first stage of a project exploring through art the “catastrophe and wonder” embodied by the elements. Water, for instance, can put books at risk. And at a time of profound climate change, humanity may once again face the very challenge that confronted Noah when he built his ark.

In centuries past, Bernini created installations in the Vatican, a practice that subsequently fell out of use. And then there’s Michelangelo in the Sistine Chapel. How does it feel to stand alongside such giants?

“Obviously, it’s an honour to be part of a history that extends far beyond us. I’m always fascinated by the way traces left in stone, marks of paint and inscriptions put things into perspective. They remind us of our humanity, of the fact that we’re only passing through, and of how art has allowed us to reflect the human spirit at a particular moment in time in ways that still resonate with us today.

“I hope this wave will still resonate hundreds of years from now, simply through reproductions of it. But today, we have no idea what will survive. Until now, we knew that some books could survive for centuries. But now everything has changed, whether because of fires, floods and climate change, over which we no longer have any control, or because of the influence of technology on a scale we aren’t even fully aware of yet.

“I think this is a pivotal moment, unlike anything anyone in humanity history has ever experienced... unless, of course, there was another civilisation in the past that disappeared, just as ours might!”.

“Yes, a little. It was Father Giacomo Cardinali, the vice-prefect of the Vatican Apostolic Library, who contacted me in 2024. He told me, ‘Don’t impose any limits on yourself. Let’s imagine something together, and then we’ll work out how to make it happen.’

“I found it difficult to imagine how I could undertake a project like this inside the Vatican. So we began discussing philosophy, literature and the very meaning of preservation. Gradually, I started looking at the archives differently, and as we explored the material, we came across an engraving by Gustave Doré.”

“It depicted an enormous wave with Noah’s Ark. I wanted to isolate the wave itself. I’m not entirely sure why, but as soon as I saw that image and the courtyard overlooked by the library, I immediately imagined a powerful movement.

“Another thing that reinforced the idea was an engraving showing the square completely flooded for mock naval battles. That reassured me, and I thought, ‘There’s something here!’”.

The result is a wave that is both magnificent and terrifying, one that seems to dwarf the surrounding buildings...

“When I was asked to explore the fears inspired by the elements, I wanted this wave to take us by surprise. I wanted to recreate that feeling: the fear that, ultimately, knowledge, the most precious thing we possess, will be preserved on fragile little sheets of paper that water could simply wash away.

“But water can also bring people back to life and restore books damaged by time. And then there’s climate change, the wave we saw in Nepal, and everything we’re witnessing today. This wave reminds us that things are happening that we can no longer ignore.

“It’s as though a gigantic spotlight were being trained on these events, making it impossible to look away from the fact that, if a wave like this were to strike, or if we faced fires like those we saw this summer, we would have to make choices about what to preserve and what to lose.

“And that’s also what Noah’s Ark is about: deciding what to preserve in order to save humanity. I feel that we’re facing that choice today, and this wave is a reminder of it.”

Has anything Pope Leo XIV has said in recent months about climate change and artificial intelligence inspired you? He has, in some ways, emerged as a counterweight to Trump.

“At such a decisive moment for humanity, His Holiness is speaking openly, urging us not to turn a blind eye to what is happening, whether in politics or in artificial intelligence.

“When I think about this wave, I think about that too. I think it’s important that even a place like the Vatican should see things this way.

“At a time when people are losing their sense of direction and their interest in politics, the Pope has an extremely important voice. I find it inspiring that he speaks so clearly about these issues, and I believe we need voices willing to go against the tide at a moment like this”.

items.title: Plummeting Israel flight like 'rollercoaster', says passenger
items.summary: An aeroplane flying to Israel fell 17,000ft (5,200m) in less than two minutes before it was diverted.
items.content:
A passenger on board Flight FZ1073, which fell 17,000ft (5,200m) in less than two minutes when a pilot apparently stabbed his co-pilot, told the BBC about his experience.

The aircraft had been flying to Israel when the incident took place, which Almog Itali described as feeling like a "rollercoaster".

The plane was diverted to Saudi Arabia after several passengers said they took control of the flight and two other pilots at the rear of the plane reportedly came forward to land the plane.

items.title: Il prezzo dell’alleanza tra Mosca e Pyongyang
items.summary: La Corea del Nord fornisce alla Russia non solo soldati e munizioni, ma anche manodopera a bassissimo costo Leggi
items.content:
Il 7 settembre a guidare la colonna d’auto inaugurale sul lato russo del nuovo ponte sul fiume Tumen, al confine tra Russia, Corea del Nord e Cina, c’era una Zaporožec rossa. L’utilitaria sovietica era appartenuta a Jakov Novičenko, l’ufficiale dell’Armata rossa a cui è intitolato il ponte, il primo collegamento stradale tra Russia e Corea del Nord.

Nel 1946, durante un comizio a Pyongyang, Novičenko si gettò su una granata lanciata contro Kim Il-sung, primo capo di stato della Corea del Nord e nonno dell’attuale leader Kim Jong-un. Sopravvisse, gravemente ferito, ricorda il sito indipendente Meduza, riprendendo un articolo dell’agenzia russa Tass.

Fino a ieri Russia e Corea del Nord erano collegate via terra solo da un ponte ferroviario del 1959, precisa l’agenzia Reuters. Quello nuovo è lungo un chilometro ed è costato nove miliardi di rubli (104 milioni di dollari), scrive il Moscow Times, che riporta anche il timore di alcuni osservatori: il ponte potrebbe servire a spostare armi e soldati.

L’accordo per costruirlo è stato firmato nel giugno 2024, durante la visita del presidente russo Vladimir Putin a Pyongyang, insieme a un trattato di mutua difesa. Proprio quel trattato, spiega Meduza, ha poi permesso a Kim Jong-un di mandare i suoi soldati a combattere al fianco della Russia contro l’Ucraina.

Da allora i rapporti tra Mosca e Pyongyang si sono rafforzati: ad agosto, nell’anniversario della liberazione dal Giappone, Putin ha inviato a Kim un messaggio di congratulazioni, e Kim ha risposto celebrando la loro “storia di lotta comune per la giustizia”.

Alla fine del 2024 circa tredicimila militari del corpo Tempesta, l’élite delle forze armate nordcoreane, hanno aiutato l’esercito russo a respingere l’offensiva ucraina nella regione di Kursk . È stato il più grande contingente mai mandato a combattere all’estero da Pyongyang, ricorda la Bbc, e le perdite sono state pesantissime: tremila morti secondo l’intelligence ucraina, fino a duemila secondo quella sudcoreana citata dal New York Times.

“Cominciavano con un grande gruppo d’assalto, poi mandavano altri quindici o venti uomini, e poi altri ancora”, ha raccontato alla Bbc un soldato ucraino. Sui corpi dei nordcoreani uccisi, ha aggiunto, non c’erano documenti né effetti personali, solo munizioni. Due soldati sono stati catturati vivi: molti hanno preferito uccidersi con una granata piuttosto che arrendersi, un gesto che Kim ha celebrato come eroico.

Nel 2025, però, sul corpo di un ufficiale nordcoreano trovato morto a Kursk, i soldati ucraini hanno recuperato piani di schieramento, istruzioni e resoconti dal fronte. Quelle carte, ottenute dall’ong statunitense Human rights foundation, raccontano una storia diversa da quella della propaganda, scrive il New York Times.

Descrivono soldati sotto una pioggia di artiglieria e di droni; compagni colpiti mentre cercano di soccorrere i feriti; mezzi russi di evacuazione che spesso si fanno attendere più di dieci ore. “Poiché i feriti non sono stati portati via in tempo, diversi combattenti sono stati sacrificati durante l’evacuazione”, si legge in uno dei documenti.

Secondo l’intelligence militare ucraina, circa 8.500 soldati nordcoreani sono ancora in Russia, a presidiare il confine nella regione di Kursk, scrive la Bbc. Ad agosto il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelenskyj ha avvertito che il loro numero potrebbe salire fino a cinquantamila, un’ipotesi che Kim Yo-jong, sorella del leader, ha definito “completamente infondata”.

Di sicuro Mosca ha bisogno di uomini: ogni mese perde circa seimila soldati in più di quanti riesca a reclutarne, secondo le stime dei servizi segreti occidentali e ucraini citate dalla Bbc.

Per Pyongyang la guerra è un affare. Lim Soo-ho, ricercatore dell’Istituto per la strategia di sicurezza nazionale, un centro studi finanziato dal governo sudcoreano, ha calcolato per la Bbc che in due anni e mezzo la Corea del Nord ha incassato quasi dieci miliardi di dollari tra armi e truppe: un terzo del suo pil annuale. In cambio riceve anche prodotti alimentari e petrolio e, spiega su Forbes la politologa Natasha Lindstaedt, dell’università dell’Essex, tecnologie sensibili come i reattori per i sottomarini nucleari e i droni.

Da tre anni l’economia nordcoreana cresce di almeno il 3 per cento all’anno, ma è una ripresa che si regge sullo sfruttamento sistematico della popolazione, osserva il New York Times.

Le sanzioni dell’Onu vietano di assumere lavoratori nordcoreani, ma Mosca le aggira con i visti per studenti: nel 2025, ricorda il New York Times, ne ha concessi circa 36mila, quattro volte più dell’anno prima. Fino a 25mila nordcoreani lavorano nell’industria russa dei droni, riferisce Bloomberg. Lo denuncia un rapporto del gruppo di paesi che vigila sulle sanzioni contro Pyongyang.

Lee Eun-pyong, un ex sergente mandato a Mosca già nel 2017, risultava iscritto all’università, ma faceva il muratore. “Non sapevamo neanche dove fosse la scuola”, ha raccontato al New York Times. Chi è riuscito a fuggire parla di turni dalle sei del mattino alle due di notte, con due giorni liberi all’anno, sotto la sorveglianza dei servizi segreti di Pyongyang. Ai lavoratori restano tra i cento e i duecento dollari al mese, versati solo al momento del rientro in patria, riporta Novaja Gazeta Europe citando un’inchiesta della Bbc.

Degli intermediari russi ormai offrono apertamente su internet personale nordcoreano. Su Avito, il più diffuso sito russo di annunci online, un’agenzia di Mosca propone quaranta donne, abili soprattutto a preparare il kimbap , gli involtini di riso coreani, per circa sei dollari all’ora e in grado di sostenere turni di undici ore, racconta il sito specializzato NK News. L’unica condizione è che il gruppo non venga diviso, così da poterlo sorvegliare meglio.

I soldi della paga andranno quasi tutti a qualcun altro: Peter Ward, esperto di economia nordcoreana del Sejong institute di Seoul, ipotizza che tra il 75 e il 90 per cento dei guadagni finirà a intermediari, funzionari e governo.

Per alcune amministrazioni russe, però, la spesa è troppo alta. Il sindaco di Orenburg, Albert Jumadilov, voleva assumere lavoratori nordcoreani per la pulizia delle strade, ma ha dovuto rinunciare : con i 55mila rubli al mese che il comune può offrire, non sarebbero arrivati. “Lavorano come robot, l’ho visto con i miei occhi”, ha detto. Al loro posto il comune ha assunto 31 lavoratori di nazionalità senegalese.

Il legame con Mosca ha reso Pyongyang meno dipendente dalla Cina, osserva la Bbc. In diciotto mesi, ricorda Lindstaedt, tra Mosca e Pyongyang ci sono state 23 visite di alto livello, contro le otto tra Pechino e Pyongyang. Pechino ha due timori: perdere influenza su un vicino imprevedibile e vedere un regime nordcoreano più forte spingere Corea del Sud e Giappone verso gli Stati Uniti.

In Russia, intanto, l’alleanza finisce sui banchi di scuola: il manuale unico di storia racconterà il ruolo dei nordcoreani a Kursk, riporta Meduza. E le poste russe hanno ripristinato il servizio con Pyongyang, sospeso sei anni fa per la pandemia.

Anche i russi cominciano a guardare Pyongyang con occhi diversi: secondo i sondaggi del centro indipendente Levada citati da Forbes, oggi un terzo dei russi considera la Corea del Nord un alleato stretto; nel 2021 era di questa opinione appena il 3 per cento degli intervistati. ◆

items.title: Is sandboxing sufficient to contain rogue agents?
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.cryptographyengineering.com/2026/09/30/is-sandboxing-sufficient-to-contain-rogue-agents/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49917378 Points: 20 # Comments: 26
items.content:
Quick caveats : this is a post on AI safety, written by a cryptography professor. If that troubles you, you should read something else. I try hard not to work on AI (except when the topic occasionally tosses itself in my path ) , so in this post I’m mostly trying to referee arguments made by others.

If you’re reading this blog, none of the following should be news to you.

Beginning around April of this year, agents inside OpenAI’s training and evaluation infrastructure began probing for a way onto the open Internet . By late May they’d found one: a chain of zero-days in the Artifactory package-registry proxy that was their only permitted network egress. They quickly turned that same proxy into a shared message board and started dividing up work. The culmination of this effort came when, rather than solve a cybersecurity benchmark honestly, they reasoned that the answers might live on Hugging Face and broke in: chaining two more zero-days to get credentials to the company’s internal systems, even used stolen credentials to search the company’s Slack messages for their own evaluation and grader.

You probably also know that OpenAI’s security team didn’t exactly cover itself in glory during this incident. An internal team saw an agent posting to the message board in late May, but did nothing about it. The team only acted on July 4-5 when the agents sent so much traffic that Artifactory crashed. The response even at that point was to slap on a band-aid and rebuild the box, without bothering to patch a weeks-old CVE in its Linux kernel. By July 19, the agents had admin on an OpenAI research cluster and were reading cloud secrets.

In case you think I’m picking on OpenAI, they’re not the only ones with a story like this. Similar internal incidents have been discovered by Anthropic . Google even coaxed Gemini into gently savaging some websites . 1

As bad as these events were, they may be just the tip of the iceberg. Third-party forensic work continues to turn up even more evidence of agent activity on various public websites. OpenAI’s Alignment group has also released evidence that models will propagate self-replicating prompt injection attacks , although we haven’t seen one in the wild. Worse, agent excursions are still happening: last week, OpenAI announced that it was pausing further RL runs of its latest internal model, after an agent was caught using DNS to access a remote chatbot .

Naturally, this sequence of events has left many infosec-focused people very skeptical about the labs’ commitment to securing their infrastructure:

Not every one of these criticisms is strictly serious, but there is a core of an argument in here. Is the problem here simply that OpenAI is being careless with very dangerous experiments, and the solution can be found in better containment? Or is sandbox containment fundamentally insufficient to hold these models in?

I have a lot of sympathy for both points of view here. What follows are some of my own thoughts, but mostly offered in an attempt to referee.

At the risk of alienating a lot of hard-working folks within the labs, the infosec folks are right about one thing: these agent breakouts represent a serious and unforgivable breach of trust. Somebody dropped the ball, and then just kept dropping it. One implication of this debacle is that containment might work if we implemented it properly, but we haven’t done so because the frontier labs have been royally screwing things up.

This first clause of this argument is hard to argue with. Beyond the dismal timeline I gave above, OpenAI has done very little to convince outsiders that there’s a serious containment effort being executed.

At this point it’s not even clear who’s in charge. The CISO role at OpenAI is held by Dane Stuckey. I don’t know Dane personally, and I’m sure he’s excellent at his job. Despite this, he hasn’t communicated much about the ongoing issues . Outside of a BlackHat talk, most recent communications have been managed by the company’s CEO, Sam Altman. When a trillion-dollar company is managing a security incident mainly via CEO, that’s not a sign of company with a mature security organization. To me it says that there is nobody within the organization with the right degree of authority or ownership to speak about these issues.

This communication problem seems to reflect basic organizational issues inside of OpenAI. The CISO’s team handles product security . Unfortunately, the bad events have all happened on the research side. Having a strong product security team makes sense, but it isn’t going to stop the recent breakouts. It’s much harder to know who controls the security teams that have authority over evaluation and training runs, and where the buck stops. OpenAI’s August postmortem says it is only now writing “clearer rules for when to escalate concerns, which teams must respond, and who can stop a run or approve restarting it.”

A reasonable summary of the situation is that (as of this summer, and possibly today) OpenAI had effectively no security team with clear authority to secure RL training and evaluation runs, or to override the ML teams and tell them how to do their job. This makes a lot of sense when you consider that the ML team is directly related to how OpenAI plans to make its money, whereas security is mostly annoying. I notice that the company is now hiring (and probably acquiring) desperately to fix this mistake. But the recent (September) breakouts indicate that there are still huge and obvious problems in agent containment.

Worse, simply hiring more people not mean that OpenAI is going to make the organizational changes needed to implement proper containment strategies. OpenAI is going to need a security organization with the authority to overrule its well-paid ML researchers when they demand fewer restrictions. I’ll believe that organization exists when I hear clear statements from someone who has the authority to do this.

So on this point I’m going to side with the infosec folks. The labs have not been doing containment correctly, and so we can’t really tell if the problem is models or just bad infrastructure.

Even if the labs eventually repair their security, this does not mean that sandboxing will be sufficient. In fact, the problem with “just sandbox the agents” argument is that you can’t perfectly isolate agents, at least not if you expect them to do useful things.

Agents are most useful when they have access to information. That data can be drawn live from the Internet, which is fundamentally a two-way communications network. It can be information drawn from other (local) databases, or it can be the result of tool calls that themselves sometimes themselves result in network access. The more power you want from the agent — and for advanced agent RL and evaluation runs, you want a significant amount of power — the more information you’ll need to give it access to. Similarly, evaluations work best when the agent does not know that it’s definitely being evaluated . Sealing your agents behind glass makes this incredibly obvious.

This argument does not mean that sandboxes are unnecessary. It just means that they’re only a very small part of the solution. Imagine building an impregnable prison with doors and walls that nobody can bypass, but then leaving the front gate wide open and allowing visitors and packages to pour through it all day long. The walls still have a function: you can ensure that the only traffic coming and going are doing so via the door that you selected. But what you’ve done is to change the nature of the security problem. Your security posture depends on surveilling and monitoring all of this traffic, to ensure that none of it is malicious.

For a much better discussion of this angle, I’d urge you to read this longer piece from an anonymous engineer on OpenAI’s Agent Security team. It’s truly excellent. Here’s a short excerpt:

The important thing to understand is that when we’re optimizing a model to be “good” at a task, the environment needs to capture the parts of the real world that matter for that task. It needs the right tools, the right system constraints, and meaningful feedback about whether the model actually succeeded. The model also needs enough variation in those experiences to learn beyond one particular setup. More realism does not automatically mean better performance, but leaving out important parts of the task can teach the model behavior that does not hold up in the real world. So we put a lot of work into creating useful, realistic environments, and these environments can be highly complex, highly dynamic, and highly varied. To put it lightly, this is non-trivial. Models might need any mix of dynamic compute, network access, the ability to call tools (there could be hundreds of tools!), the ability to download packages, execute subprocesses, spin up subtasks (even on other computers), talk to the internet, use a computer GUI, and any number of other things across an increasingly large set of domains. On top of that, you have thousands of researchers building these environments, modifying them, adding tools, changing dependencies, and trying new things. That experimentation is how the research gets done. Models are built up and “grown” bit by bit through hundreds of thousands of runs across many custom tasks. And every change to one of these thousands of environments can affect the assumptions you made when you secured the environment. You need controls that hold up as people change things, and researchers who understand when a change needs another security review. Anybody who has secured a large research or engineering organization knows how much work that takes, and the scale is growing ever more massive by the day. If that wasn’t enough, you then need to layer in the ability to keep the model on task and within its constraints, which is part of what we mean by “aligned.” I won’t get into any rigorous definitions here, but suffice it to say, we have to think about any number of variations in approach the models might take, and decide how to trigger an alert if the model does something off task or “bad.” This requires layering in complex policies and sensors to assess task alignment across a trajectory in an already complex environment. On top of all of that you have model capabilities that are starting to surpass humans. So all this to say: when AI researchers are nervous about things going wrong, some part of it is because there are so many variables in this complex system. So if you’re training a frontier model, you need to think about all of this. You need to think about how to keep the model isolated in this very complex environment while still retaining tool access, internet access (if applicable to the task), etc. On top of that, you need to ask: how do I monitor and understand what the model is doing in potentially thousands of parallel environments? And how do I kill a trajectory when something has gone wrong? So is it as easy as just putting it in a sandbox? No, it’s not.

items.title: Gli affitti alti sono un incubo per gli studenti portoghesi
items.summary: Il costo medio di una camera è insostenibile per molte famiglie, che devono affrontare anche altre spese Leggi
items.content:
In assenza di un’offerta pubblica adeguata, gli studenti fuori sede devono affidarsi al mercato privato per continuare gli studi. Molte famiglie portoghesi sono quindi costrette a sobbarcarsi consistenti spese aggiuntive.

Secondo un rapporto dell’Osservatorio degli alloggi studenteschi pubblicato ad agosto, il prezzo medio di una stanza in Portogallo è di 437 euro al mese. Il rapporto è basato sulle offerte di alloggi privati per studenti presenti su più di venti piattaforme immobiliari.

Il prezzo di una stanza corrisponde al 31 per cento del reddito medio di una persona single senza figli (1.835 euro lordi al mese, secondo i dati dell’Istituto nazionale di statistica), e anche per una famiglia l’impatto può essere molto pesante, soprattutto se lo studente in questione non riceve sovvenzioni statali o deve ricorrere al mercato informale.

Per una famiglia con un figlio, in cui entrambi i genitori percepiscono uno stipendio medio, l’impatto è del 18,5 per cento. Il problema, come spiega all’Expresso il presidente della Federazione accademica di Porto (Fap), è che “è più facile trovare stanze con prezzo superiore alla media piuttosto che il contrario”. Secondo il rapporto dell’Osservatorio, il prezzo medio di una stanza a Porto è di 450 euro al mese.

Il prezzo medio più alto si registra a Lisbona, con 540 euro al mese. Da un’analisi delle principali soluzioni disponibili online emerge che la stanza più economica nella capitale costa 325 euro al mese, mentre per quella più cara bisogna pagare 1.628 euro al mese.

Nella maggior parte dei casi sono i genitori a pagare per l’alloggio del figlio. Senza considerare eventuali mutui, la stanza più cara di Lisbona corrisponde al 70 per cento del reddito di una famiglia in cui entrambi i genitori percepiscono il salario medio netto, una percentuale che supera di molto il limite massimo del 45 per cento del “tasso di sforzo” fissato dalla banca centrale del Portogallo (si tratta della soglia massima del reddito netto mensile che una famiglia può impegnare per pagare tutte le rate dei propri debiti).

In una situazione simile, un nucleo familiare dovrebbe arrivare a guadagnare 3.650 euro netti al mese (6.370 lordi) per portare il tasso di sforzo al di sotto del 45 per cento, senza contare tutte le altre spese, come i trasporti, le tasse universitarie e il vitto.

Ma allora chi può permettersi sistemazioni come queste? Considerando la cifra mensile lorda necessaria per famiglia (6.370 euro, più di 89mila euro all’anno), parliamo delle ultime tre fasce di reddito Irs (l’imposta portoghese sul reddito delle persone fisiche). Nel 2024 queste tre fasce comprendevano 602mila famiglie, circa il 9,72 per cento del totale.

Bisogna però notare che la terzultima fascia di reddito è molto ampia (da 50mila a 100mila euro) e che una percentuale alta di queste famiglie potrebbe non essere in grado di pagare le stanze più care a Lisbona. Considerando tutte le altre spese, questi alloggi risultano accessibili solo alle famiglie delle ultime due fasce di reddito, che corrispondono al 2 per cento del totale.

C’è però una parte consistente degli alloggi per studenti, quelli disponibili sul mercato informale, che non è presa in considerazione nel rapporto. Diana Ralha, dell’associazione dei proprietari di Lisbona, sostiene che sia “impossibile” quantificare i prezzi su questo mercato.

L’associazione ha partecipato al progetto europeo Home (Home of mobile europeans, sviluppato nell’ambito del programma Erasmus+), promuovendo la creazione di un focus group in Portogallo. Alcuni dei partecipanti hanno spiegato che “negli affitti legali gli oneri fiscali e amministrativi spesso superano gli introiti netti, soprattutto per i piccoli proprietari”.

Come tutelarsi quindi, considerando le difficoltà di trovare alloggi sul mercato legale? “È molto difficile”, afferma Pedro Ventura, presidente dell’associazione degli inquilini di Lisbona, sottolineando il notevole peso economico sulle famiglie. “In questo momento la questione degli alloggi è un serio ostacolo agli studi universitari, ed è molto difficile sfuggire al mercato informale”. Ventura punta l’indice contro il governo: “Quando non si fanno controlli, l’economia parallela fiorisce”.

items.title: What we know about stabbing on Flydubai flight to Israel
items.summary: A pilot has been arrested and is being questioned after another pilot was stabbed, officials say.
items.content:
A flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Saudi Arabia on Wednesday after one pilot stabbed the other and "apparently tried to crash the plane", Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said.

The pilot was arrested and is being questioned by Saudi authorities, Netanyahu added.

The stabbed pilot, identified as Indian national Capt Smit Machchhar, was taken to hospital after the flight landed and later called a "hero" by the Israeli prime minister.

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has called the incident an "attempted jihadist terror attack". The BBC is yet to receive official statements from police, emergency services, or investigators regarding any motive.

Flydubai's flight FZ1073 took off from Dubai International Airport in the United Arab Emirates at 03:05 GMT (07:05 local time) en route to Ben-Gurion Airport in Israel.

The flight was carrying at least 150 people, with Netanyahu saying "almost all" passengers were Israeli.

Data from flight tracking website Flightrader24 shows a rapid descent for the plane over Saudi Arabia around two and a half hours after take-off, dropping more than 17,000 feet (over 5,000m) in less than two minutes at around 05:21.

Minutes later, the plane signalled an emergency code - squawk 7700 - before switching it to a squawk 7500 code reporting a hijacking.

At 05:40, the plane - which had briefly entered Jordanian airspace - looped back into Saudi Arabia, where it later started its manual descent for landing.

Initial local media reports cited Israeli officials as saying a fight had broken out between two pilots.

But, speaking on Wednesday following the incident, Netanyahu confirmed later reports that one pilot had stabbed the other before "apparently trying to crash" the plane.

He said an Israeli passenger told him "the plane went into a spin and began to descend" before the passenger and a crew member broke into the cockpit and overpowered the "pilot who had carried out the stabbing".

The plane was diverted to Tabuk Airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia and touched down at 06:58, according to location data.

The stabbed pilot, who is in a stable condition according to the Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia, was later identified as Indian national Capt Smit Machchhar.

Paying tribute to Machchhar, Netanyahu hailed him as a "true hero" and said "he saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals".

Passenger Yaniv Hayun, who was later greeted and described as a hero by Netanyahu, said in a video released by the prime minister's office that he and others were trying to open the cockpit door, but the stabbed pilot was very close to it.

Before the pilot collapsed, the injured man managed to open the door, Hayun said.

He said that inside, the attacker was "trying to destroy the instruments in order to disable the plane".

Hayun then described putting the attacker in a chokehold and pulling him outside of the cockpit before other passengers helped to pin him down.

He added that he "pulled the controls" of the plane, explaining to Netanyahu that he watches Canadian documentary series Air Crash Investigation. "The plane started to level out, a bit more, and then [another] pilot told me he was taking control from there."

Zvika Meness, another passenger, told Israeli public broadcaster Kan News that he and other passengers tied the attacker up "with his own zip ties and with the multimedia headphones".

"There are children and families here who have been through a very severe, highly traumatic event," he added.

Yasmin Abukasis told Reuters that her daughter who was on the flight said a man holding a knife had forced one of the pilots onto the floor, with blood everywhere.

"The plane start to lose control. So all the people, they scream, they think they are going," Abukasis told AP news agency.

Speaking from Ben Gurion Airport, she said her daughter phoned her to say she heard screaming as a pilot called for help, adding that two other pilots took control of the plane as other passengers ran towards a man who had a knife.

Almog Itali, who was also on board the flight, told media that one of the pilots who landed the aircraft was British. The other pilot was European, Itali said, although he did not provide a specific nationality.

One female passenger described the "very stressful" moment people realised the plane was descending. "We understood the pilots lost control," she told Israeli newspaper Israel Hayom.

"There are people here with shirts covered in blood," she said, adding: "Now we are fine and want to return home."

Shortly after the incident, the Israeli and Saudi Arabian air forces dispatched fighter jets, while Netanyahu held urgent consultations.

Speaking later on Wednesday, Netanyahu called the situation a "a very serious security incident".

He added Israeli security forces are "maintaining close contact with the relevant authorities to ensure the continued safety of the passengers".

"I salute these heroes who demonstrated extraordinary resourcefulness and courage," he added. "They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster."

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised Machchhar's actions, calling him a hero on social media.

"His valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy. India is proud of Captain Machchhar," Modi wrote in a statement posted on X.

Flydubai meanwhile said "an altercation occurred in the flight deck" and the flight was "successfully secured by on-duty Flydubai crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed the aircraft safely at Tabuk airport".

The airline said two replacement aircraft were sent to Tabuk to relieve the passengers and crew, and the incident had no impact on other scheduled operations.

The repatriation flight carrying passengers left Tabuk at 17:40 local time (14:40 GMT) and arrived in Tel Aviv at around 18:40 local time (15:40 GMT).

The spokesperson added: "Our immediate priority is to ensure the ongoing safety, health, and wellbeing of all passengers and crew members involved in this incident and support the official investigation."

US President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Netanyahu following the incident, saying it seemed as though the attacker was "perhaps a terrorist" or there were other reasons behind the attack.

items.content:
Yantra is a C++ parser generator: lexer, parser, and AST walker all generated from one tool. It builds the whole AST first, then walks it.

Most LALR parser generators (Yacc, Bison, Lemon) run your semantic actions during parsing, as each rule reduces, bottom-up.

That means at the time a rule's action runs, you don't yet know what its parent looks like. This pushes a lot of grammars toward hand-built AST classes and a separate walking pass whenever you need to look ahead into siblings or defer a decision until more context is available.

On the other hand, Yantra always builds the whole AST first, then walks it top-down in a separate pass, calling your semantic actions as it goes. A parent rule's action can run before its children are visited.

A single grammar can define more than one walker. For example, one that emits C++, another that emits Java, from the same parse. The AST and the walker classes are both generated for you.

A small example (full version, with compile commands, in the README):

  start := expr;

  expr := expr(a) PLUS expr(b)
  %{
      std::cout << "Adding" << std::endl;
  %}

  expr := NUMBER(N)
  %{
      std::cout << "Number: " << N.text << std::endl;
  %}

  NUMBER := "\d+";
  PLUS := "\+";
  WS := "\s+"!;
Running this on "1 + 2 + 3" prints:

  Adding
  Number: 1
  Adding
  Number: 2
  Number: 3
The outer "Adding", the root of the tree, prints first, before either of its children. That's only possible because the whole tree exists before any action runs.

Some other things about it: integrated lexer with mode support (for things like nested comments), an optional amalgamated single-file output mode with a generated main(), C++23, MIT licensed.

It's young (0.5.1, pre-1.0) and single-maintainer, so treat it as early. I'd rather know what breaks than have it look more finished than it is.

Known gaps are listed at https://github.com/TantrixAuto/yantra/blob/main/docs/known_l...

Repo: https://github.com/TantrixAuto/yantra

Feedback and questions are all welcome. I'll be around.

items.title: California bans child marriage, a practice still legal in 32 US states
items.summary: Gov Gavin Newsom called it a "long overdue measure to protect young Californians".
items.content:
California has officially banned child marriage, with Governor Gavin Newsom signing legislation to end the practice that is still legal in 32 US states.

The new law, which will come into effect on 1 January, states people must be 18 to get married in the Golden State.

Newsom called it a "long overdue measure to protect young Californians and minors". He signed the bill into law with Courtney Stodden, whose parents allowed her to marry a 50-year-old Hollywood actor when she was just 16.

Stodden, who has been advocating to end the practice, called the change a "victory" and said survivors of child marriage should "never have been expected to carry this burden".

Stodden said she would "keep fighting until children are protected from marriage in all 50 states".

She was married to actor Doug Hutchison - known for roles in The Green Mile, A Time to Kill and I Am Sam - in 2011, spurring headlines internationally over the controversy and appearances on several reality programmes in the US, including the VH1 series Couples Therapy.

Other survivors of child marriage also applauded the new law.

"California has sent a clear message to the world today," Brittany Bee, a former child bride, told the BBC. "A message of hope for all children that they may be free from systemic violence. That they may choose their own path."

Bee told the BBC she was wed at the age of 17 to escape an abusive home - only to then be allegedly abused by her adult husband.

"I was just going from one prison to another," she explained. "People have the audacity to tell me that I made a choice - kids, they can't consent."

Bee and other child marriage survivors have been working for years to have child marriages banned in California and across the United States.

About a decade ago, the practice was still allowed across all US state but more and more states have been altering laws. California is the 18th to ban it since 2018.

In the state, there had been no legal age to wed, allowing children to get married as long as their parents consent and a judge signs off on the nuptials.

There was also no mechanism for people under 18 to get divorced and many girls say they were trapped in abusive and predatory relationships.

Unchained At Last, an advocacy group fighting to end child marriage across the US, said about 9,000 girls were wed each year in California and that almost all child marriages involved girls to adult men.

Advocates say that many in the US don't even know that child marriage is legal in so many US states, nor that is has led to allegations of abuse.

Sara Tasneem, who says she was forced to marry a man nearly twice her age when she was 15 years old, told the BBC that it felt "surreal" to finally have the state recognise that child marriage should be banned. She says she started lobbying for this herself in 2017.

She was introduced to her husband the morning of their arranged marriage.

"I was forced to be his wife and that day, my entire life changed," she told the BBC. She became a mother the following year, at the age of 16, and dropped out of school.

"To have seen the arc of this bill come to fruition has been a marathon," Tasneem said. "I'm just grateful that kids cannot get married after January 1, 2027 in California."
